experiments.name: Copying FOMO app traders
experiments.question: Can we front-run or copy the best FOMO app wallets?
experiments.method: On-chain audit of 60+ wallets, 7-day forward test
experiments.result: Winners churn; copying after the fact loses to fees and slippage.
experiments.public_title: Copy the best wallets on FOMO app
experiments.hypothesis: Following top traders' buys a few seconds late still makes money.
experiments.efficacy: Copies lost: the edge was speed, and fees ate the rest.

experiments.name: Technical signals on liquid memecoins
experiments.question: Does any TA entry beat random in 27 liquid memecoins?
experiments.method: 90 days, out-of-sample half, random-entry control
experiments.result: Every strategy lost 2–5% per trade; none beat random.
experiments.hypothesis: Classic chart signals (breakouts, moving averages, RSI) can time liquid memecoins.
experiments.efficacy: 27 coins, 90 days: every signal lost 2–5% per trade, none beat random entries.

experiments.name: Tweet sniper on fresh launches
experiments.question: Do influencer tweets predict pumps early enough to buy?
experiments.method: Dataset of tweets vs. 6h outcomes, shadow run
experiments.result: Signals arrive after the move; snipers own the first minutes.
experiments.hypothesis: Buying a new token right after a big account tweets it is profitable.
experiments.efficacy: The move happens before the tweet reaches us. Discarded.

experiments.name: Anti-rug: common-funder clustering
experiments.question: Can we detect rugs by tracing who funded the top holders?
experiments.method: Helius funded-by on top-20 holders + deployer history, applied live
experiments.result: Caught 3 concentrated tokens before buying (CHICO, tSpaceX, LMAO!).
experiments.hypothesis: Tracing who funded a token's top holders exposes rugs before they happen.
experiments.efficacy: Blocked 3 concentrated tokens before buying (CHICO, tSpaceX, LMAO!). In use on every buy.

experiments.name: Perps signals on Hyperliquid
experiments.question: Any short-term long/short edge in perps (funding, cascades, breakouts, pairs)?
experiments.method: 34 markets, 90 days, real funding, out-of-sample, random control
experiments.result: None passed (t ≥ 2.5 and beat random). Volume breakouts lose clearly (−1.5%/trade).
experiments.hypothesis: Funding extremes, liquidation cascades or breakouts predict the next 12–48 hours on perps.
experiments.efficacy: 34 markets, 90 days, ~1,800 simulated trades: none beat random. Breakouts lost 1.5% per trade.

experiments.name: Fast momentum in $300K–3M memecoins
experiments.question: Does buying small caps already up 100%+ 'on a pullback' work with 12h time stops?
experiments.method: Live, two trades
experiments.result: Both stopped out within an hour (−26%, −28%). Turned off the same night.
experiments.hypothesis: Small tokens already up 100%+ keep running if bought on a pullback.
experiments.efficacy: Both live trades stopped out within an hour (−26%, −28%). Turned off the same night.

experiments.name: Stops that only move up
experiments.question: Does ratcheting the stop with the peak keep more of the winners?
experiments.method: Live on GTA6/REMUS; rules 1.3x→entry, 1.6x→75% of peak
experiments.result: REMUS closed +14% instead of round-tripping; GTA6 protected at 1.3x.
experiments.hypothesis: Raising the stop as a position climbs keeps more of each winner.
experiments.efficacy: REMUS closed +14% instead of giving it back; GTA6 is protected far above its entry. In use.

experiments.name: Volatility targeting + drawdown throttle
experiments.question: Does sizing each pocket to a fixed volatility (and cutting exposure after a drawdown) improve risk-adjusted results?
experiments.method: Replay pocket signals fixed-size vs vol-targeted (10/20-day half-life); same costs; random-entry control
experiments.result: Oct 30 backtest (majors_bt.py, 8 majors 2020–26, out-of-sample 2024–26): sizing each position to 60% annual volatility raised out-of-sample Sharpe in every trend variant (e.g. 20-day average long-only +0.29 → +0.72; 30-day momentum +0.50 → +0.66) and cut drawdowns.
experiments.hypothesis: Betting less when a market gets wild, and more when it calms down, cuts drawdowns without hurting returns.
experiments.efficacy: Adopted: the lab's daily-trend test sizes leverage as 60% / 30-day volatility.

experiments.name: Execution cost audit + MEV protection
experiments.question: How much of our 2–5% round trip is fee vs impact vs sandwiches, and how much can tight slippage / Jito-protected sends recover?
experiments.method: Our own 29 real memecoin fills (Oct 27–30, all plans) + 17 cash swaps: fill price vs the 1-minute market price just before (Solana Tracker candles); every memecoin fill's block read from Helius to look for a wallet trading the same pool right before AND right after us (sandwich). Then a quote-only A/B (no money): Jupiter vs Solana Tracker for 10 tokens × 3 sizes, buy and sell back (exec_cost.py, route_ab.py; ops 176–179).
experiments.result: Realized cost per side: memecoin buys median 2.5% (mean 3.4%, worst 12.7% on SAFU), sells median 1.5% (mean skewed by one GTA6 stop in a crash) → ~4% round trip median, above the 3% the protocol assumes. Sandwiches: 0 of 14 buys; 2 of 15 sells with a same-pool wallet on both sides of us, both during fast moves (GTA6 stop in a crash block with 8 traders) — ambiguous, not a systematic leak. Quotes: Jupiter and Solana Tracker give the same output (median difference 0.00%); pool round-trip cost at quote time median 1.6%. So of ~4% realized, ~1.6% is the pool, the rest is the 0.5%/side platform fee, priority fees and price drift between decision and fill. Cash swaps SOL↔USDC: ~1.0% via Solana Tracker before Oct 29 → 0.1–0.2% via Jupiter after (already live). Recommendation: use 4% round trip for memecoin backtests.
experiments.hypothesis: A big part of every memecoin trade's cost goes to bots that front-run it. Protected orders can win it back.
experiments.efficacy: Checked 29 real trades block by block: 0 of 14 buys sandwiched, 2 of 15 sells possibly (both in crash minutes). The bots are not where our money goes. Real cost is about 4% per round trip: ~1.6% is the pool itself, the rest is fees and the price moving while the order travels. Moving cash swaps to Jupiter already cut them from ~1% to ~0.15%.

experiments.name: Wash-trading / price-inflation filter
experiments.question: Do the USENIX'26 manipulation flags cut drawdowns in picks without killing winners?
experiments.method: Tag past candidates at entry; compare 7/30-day returns and >50% drawdown rate, flagged vs clean vs random same-bucket
experiments.result: Queued. Evidence: arXiv 2507.01963: 82.6% of +100% memecoins showed artificial growth; 86.7% of dumped tokens had prior manipulation
experiments.hypothesis: Tokens whose volume or price was pumped by the same wallets trading with themselves crash more often.

experiments.name: Token-unlock avoidance / short
experiments.question: Do large team/investor unlocks (>1% supply) depress price from ~30 days before?
experiments.method: Short day −30→−1 vs SOL/ETH hedge, vol-sized; control = same token, random 30-day windows
experiments.result: Queued. Evidence: Keyrock (16K unlocks, ~90% negative, team unlocks ≈ −25%); Tokenomist (236 events)
experiments.hypothesis: Tokens tend to fall in the month before large team or investor unlocks.

experiments.name: Short new perp listings after day 1
experiments.question: Do newly listed perps drift down over 7–14 days?
experiments.method: Short at day-1 close, exit d7/d14, 2x stop; pool Hyperliquid + Binance listings; control = random similar-cap perps same dates
experiments.result: Oct 30 backtest on all 114 Hyperliquid perps listed since June 2023, short at the day-1 close hedged with BTC, 0.3% costs: 60% of the shorts win and the median gain is +8% at day 7, but the average is −7% (t −1.5) because a few new listings squeeze 100%+. Random windows of the same tokens: +1.6%. The typical listing does drift down, but the tail kills the trade without a tight stop; and Jupiter Perps (our venue) only lists SOL, ETH and BTC.
experiments.hypothesis: Freshly listed perpetuals drift down over their first one to two weeks.
experiments.efficacy: Rejected for now: negative average after costs; revisit only with a stop and a venue that lists new perps.

experiments.name: Multi-lookback trend ensemble + ATR trailing stop
experiments.question: Is a 10/20/55/100-day breakout ensemble with ATR trail sturdier than the single 20-day MA?
experiments.method: Walk-forward on years of Binance daily candles; same costs/sizing; random long/short control with matched holding time
experiments.result: Oct 30 walk-forward (design 2020–23, test 2024–26, costs + funding, 100 random-timing controls): the 10-rule average is positive out of sample (long-only Sharpe +0.66, worst drop −38% vs −71% buy-and-hold) but t 1.1 < 2. 4-hour versions lose. Now live in the lab (see daily-trend test).
experiments.hypothesis: Reading the trend on four time windows at once, with a trailing stop, is sturdier than a single 20-day average.
experiments.efficacy: Testing live in the lab.

experiments.name: Smart-money breadth (not copy trading)
experiments.question: Does the change in how many historically profitable wallets hold a token predict returns?
experiments.method: Select wallets on months 1–3, test weekly rank on months 4–6; control = matched random portfolios
experiments.result: Queued. Evidence: Nansen (ETH 2020–22, self-published, no costs) — weak
experiments.public_title: Where the good wallets are moving
experiments.hypothesis: Counting how many historically profitable wallets are entering a token beats copying any single one.

experiments.name: CEX listing-announcement trade
experiments.question: Buying a Solana token on-chain at a Coinbase/Upbit/Robinhood announcement and selling at listing — still alive after 2023?
experiments.method: 2024–26 announcements; entry at +1/5/15 min, exit at listing; control = random times same tokens prior week
experiments.result: Queued. Evidence: The Tie (Coinbase n=10, +24% median day-1; shrinking since 2023); BONK/PENGU anecdotes
experiments.hypothesis: Buying a Solana token on-chain the moment a big exchange announces it, and selling at the listing, still pays.

experiments.name: Narrative + dated catalyst picks
experiments.public_title: Read the story, buy the pullback
experiments.question: Do memecoins tied to a real, dated event (e.g. the GTA VI release) outperform when bought on a pullback after an anti-rug check?
experiments.hypothesis: Memecoins riding a real event with a date keep attention long enough to run, if bought on a pullback after a clean anti-rug check.
experiments.method: Live, mesa and house book since 27/10; each pick needs a verified catalyst, liquidity ≥ $150K, real volume, clean anti-rug
experiments.result: GTA6 bought 27/10 at $0.0048: ×3.1 on 29/10 in the mesa, ×2.0 in the house book. REMUS closed +14%. LMAO!, SAPLING, SI and DOPE (no real story) are all below entry.
experiments.efficacy: Best performer so far: GTA6 ×3.1 (dated catalyst). REMUS, with a strong story but no confirmed date, +14%. Picks without a story: 0 of 4 up. Too few picks to call it yet; needs 20+.

experiments.name: Token-factory sniping (pump.fun)
experiments.question: Can we buy the launches of 'factory' creators (who graduate 15–29% of tokens) fast enough to profit?
experiments.hypothesis: Some creators launch hundreds of tokens a day and graduate far more than average; buying their launches early is profitable.
experiments.method: 3,289 launches with creator history, then a live session with 1-second candles
experiments.result: The 72% backtest win rate was an artifact: the factory buys and sells within the first seconds. Live: 1 full trade (+50%), 4 rejected by slippage.
experiments.efficacy: Only works inside block 0, against professional snipers. Discarded.

experiments.name: Respected launchers on pump.fun
experiments.question: Do creators with past graduations launch winners we can buy at minute 3?
experiments.hypothesis: Creators with a track record launch better tokens, so their next launch is worth buying early.
experiments.method: 70,789 tokens over 7 days, out-of-sample half, random control
experiments.result: Fewer rugs (−50%+ drops fell from ~65% to ~30%), but best hit rate 20% and every variant lost money after costs.
experiments.efficacy: Hit rate up from 7% to 20%, still negative per trade. Discarded.

experiments.name: News radar + news-shock short
experiments.public_title: Read the news, short the shock
experiments.question: When bearish news (exchange trouble, hacks, forced selling) is confirmed by a price drop within the hour, does a small SOL short opened within minutes and closed within hours beat its costs?
experiments.hypothesis: Macro news moves the market for hours, not seconds, so a 5-minute reaction is fast enough to catch part of the move.
experiments.method: Live in the lab wallet: fomo-radar reads RSS/CryptoPanic/X every minute, scores headlines, requires SOL -1.5% in 1h (or -2.5% in 4h, or BTC -1% in 1h), opens a 2x SOL short on Jupiter Perps (stop +3.5%, take profit -7%, 12h max). Every short is logged with entry, exit and result; shadow decisions logged too. Adopt into the book only after 20+ shocks and a result better than random timing after costs.
experiments.result: 2 live shorts closed (Oct 29–30): +$0.86 (trailing stop locked +2.5% after a best of +4.7%) and −$0.07 (breakeven stop). Needs 20+.
experiments.efficacy: 2 shocks so far: 1 win (+$0.86), 1 flat (−$0.07). Net +$0.79 on ~$20 collateral. Too early to call; needs 20+.

experiments.name: Reason-tagged post-mortem (self-review)
experiments.question: Which reasons for buying actually make money?
experiments.hypothesis: Trades bought for a verifiable story (dated catalyst, real affiliation) behave differently from trades that merely passed a numeric screen.
experiments.method: Every closed trade is tagged with the reason it was bought. An hourly review computes hit rate and average return per reason and switches off any reason with 8+ trades and a negative average until a human review re-enables it.
experiments.result: Oct 27-29: story-based picks 3 of 3 winners (+$179); screener picks 0 of 14 (about -$78); 20-day-trend buys 0 of 3 so far. Screener picks are switched off.
experiments.efficacy: Story picks: 3/3 winners. Screener picks: 0/14, -14% average. The screener is now a veto, not a trigger.

experiments.name: Flash-news meme (lab test #2, SAFU)
experiments.public_title: Buy the leader of a breaking-news meme, sell the same day
experiments.question: When a big story breaks, does the leading meme launched on it in the first 10-30 minutes pay for a same-day trade?
experiments.hypothesis: Memes born from breaking news live for hours; picking the leader early and exiting within 6 hours catches the move.
experiments.method: Live in the lab wallet, one trade: SAFU (Binance-outflow rumours, Oct 29), 0.0558 SOL, 40% stop, 6-hour time exit.
experiments.result: The pool's liquidity went to zero within hours; every sale failed (no route) and the position was written off at zero on Oct 30: about -$5.4, -100%.
experiments.efficacy: 1 trade, 0 wins, -100%. The exit never existed: the stop and the time limit cannot save a token whose pool empties.

experiments.name: Daily trend on majors, both directions (lab, Jupiter Perps)
experiments.public_title: Ride the daily trend in BTC and ETH, up or down
experiments.question: Does an average of 10 standard daily trend rules (momentum 10–90 days, price vs 20/50/100-day averages, 20/55-day breakouts), traded long or short on BTC/ETH perps and sized to volatility, beat its costs live?
experiments.hypothesis: Crypto majors trend over days to weeks, so following the daily trend both ways catches the big moves and stays out of the crashes; hour-scale moves are noise.
experiments.method: Backtest first (majors_bt.py): 8 markets, Jan 2020–Oct 2026, costs 0.10% per trade plus 10%/yr funding on longs; rules picked on 2020–23, judged on 2024–26 against 100 random-timing controls. Result: every daily trend rule was positive out of sample in 5–8 of 8 markets and cut the worst drawdown from −71% (buy and hold) to about −38%, but t-stats of 0.6–1.7 fall short of the t ≥ 2 bar; 4-hour rules, dip-buying and rip-shorting lost. Live: fomo-radar checks hourly; signal ≤ −0.5 opens a short (≥ +0.5 a long) on the more extreme of BTC/ETH, $10 collateral, leverage = 60% vol target / 30-day vol (1–2x); exit when the signal fades past ±0.2, hard stop 8% against, or 14 days. Adopt into the book after 15+ trades beating random timing.
experiments.result: Started Oct 30. First signal: ETH −0.8 (9 of 10 rules bearish), BTC −0.3.
experiments.efficacy: Testing.

experiments.name: Turtle breakout 55/20 with orders on file (book, live)
experiments.public_title: Buy the 55-day high, short the 55-day low, exit at the 20-day extreme
experiments.question: Do standing orders at each major's 55-day high (buy) and 55-day low (short), with the exit at the 20-day low/high, make money after costs?
experiments.hypothesis: Breakouts to new 55-day extremes start the multi-week moves that trend rules catch; standing orders catch them the minute they happen instead of at the daily close.
experiments.method: Backtest on 8 majors, Binance daily 2020–26, 0.1% fee per side + 0.2% slippage + 10%/yr funding on longs; out-of-sample 2024–26: long and short 148 trades, 45% winners, +7.1% per trade (t 2.04), 7 of 8 markets positive; long-only 82 trades, +13.8% (t 2.35); random entries with the same exit +1.8% (p50) / +4.3% (p95). Live from Oct 30 in the book on BTC/ETH/SOL perps at 2x, each trade sized so hitting the exit costs 1% of the book. Levels published on the book page.
experiments.result: Started Oct 30. Levels on file: short ETH at $2,233, SOL at $95.0, BTC at $74,968; buy ETH above $2,807, SOL above $124.95, BTC above $87,396.
experiments.efficacy: Testing live (passed the backtest bar).

experiments.name: Cross-market lead-lag: Nasdaq, S&P, gold, silver, dollar → crypto (hours)
experiments.public_title: Does Wall Street move first and crypto follow?
experiments.question: When the Nasdaq, S&P 500, gold, silver or the dollar make a big move, does crypto follow it in the next hours, so a trade placed after the move still wins?
experiments.hypothesis: Information starts in the bigger market and crypto takes hours to digest it: an edge from reading, not from speed.
experiments.method: 2 years of hourly bars (Yahoo futures NQ, ES, GC, SI, DXY; Binance BTC, ETH, SOL), aligned by UTC hour. Same-hour and lagged correlations; 2-sigma hourly shocks → crypto 1/3/6 h later; pre-market moves → US session; ±2% days → next 24/48 h; a short-after-shock rule with 0.12% round-trip costs. Design half / test half, random-entry control ×300.
experiments.result: Crypto moves in the SAME hour as the Nasdaq (correlation 0.43–0.47; gold 0.14–0.19; silver 0.19–0.23; dollar −0.09) and the next-hour correlation is zero everywhere (|r| ≤ 0.03), in both directions. After a 2-sigma Nasdaq drop, crypto is flat to slightly UP the next hour; shorting after the shock lost 0.1–0.5% per trade in both halves. Daily ±2% equity days were too rare for a verdict (6 in the test year); on those days crypto had already fallen 6–8% and bounced +1.5 to +3% the next day. Silver's +2% days coincided with crypto falling the next day in the test year (t −2.3) but not in the design year: one regime, not a rule.
experiments.efficacy: No lag to exploit: by the time Wall Street's move is visible, crypto has priced it. Chasing it loses after costs.

experiments.name: Memecoin swaps via Jupiter without platform fee + fill-drift log
experiments.public_title: Pay the pool, not the middleman
experiments.question: Routing memecoin buys/sells through Jupiter (no 0.5% platform fee, same pool price) and logging decision→fill drift: does realized round-trip cost drop from ~4% toward ~2.5%?
experiments.hypothesis: Our quotes are identical on both routers, so dropping the 0.5% per-side fee and trimming the delay between decision and fill should cut about 1–1.5% from every round trip.
experiments.method: Live A/B in the lab and book on alternating tickets (Jupiter vs Solana Tracker), same sizes; judge by realized cost vs the 1-minute price before (exec_cost.py) and by failure rate. Sells now log slippage, quoted impact and route (engine change Oct 30).
experiments.result: Live from Oct 30 evening: each memecoin ticket (book, lab, plans) goes through Jupiter or Solana Tracker at random, 50/50, same slippage tolerance and price guard; route logged per fill. Judge after 20+ fills per arm.
experiments.efficacy: Testing live: half of the trades go each way. Expected saving if it holds: about 1% per round trip.

experiments.name: Copy profitable perps traders (Hyperliquid, as shown in Phantom/FOMO)
experiments.question: If we copy every perp trade of wallets that were profitable in the past, do we make money after costs and a realistic copy delay?
experiments.hypothesis: Past profit (or profit per dollar traded) predicts future trades, so a filtered follower should beat random wallets.
experiments.method: Hyperliquid public leaderboard (48,306 wallets) → 300 active (150 top all-time + 150 random). Picked with days −60…−30, measured on −30…0, unlevered, equal weight per trade, 0.19% round-trip cost; last 3 days re-priced with 1-minute candles (~1 min delay). experiments/hl_copy.py, ops 191–192.
experiments.result: 76 usable traders, 5,561 out-of-sample trades: −0.19% per trade (t −2.8), 37% wins. Random wallets −0.14%; top of the leaderboard −0.53% (t −4.0); past winners −0.09%; profit/volume ≥1% −0.27%; ≥2% −0.68%. With the 1-minute delay nothing turns positive with significance. Only one wallet of the 'high hit-rate scalper' type, positive (+0.4%/trade) but n=1.
experiments.efficacy: No edge: past profit does not predict the next trades; the leaderboard top is the worst group to copy.

protocol: Out-of-sample half held out, entries at next bar open, real costs (memes ~4% round trip (measured on our own fills, Oct 30), perps 0.12% + funding), random-entry control x20; adopt only if test mean > 0, t ≥ 2.5, beats random by ≥ 0.3%/trade, design half also positive. Risk/cost changes are judged on drawdown and realized cost, not on win rate.

lab.note: A separate lab wallet, about a tenth of the house book, tests new ideas live with small size before they touch the main book.
